Subject: Redwood SDK quickstart & env setup  post-call follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today  great to learn more about TechFin's customer support use case and the low-latency chat + reranking pipeline you want to build. As promised, a short post-call recap and suggested next steps so your engineering team can get a working proof-of-concept quickly.

Recap (high level):
- Use-case: customer support assistant + relevance reranking for KB documents and short responses.
- Desired constraints: sub-200ms median latency for short queries, internal data stays in your VPC (future Dedicated/Private).
- Key integrations: embeddings index for retrieval, a lightweight reranker model, and structured tool calling for ticketing actions.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Quickstart env setup (Python + TypeScript)  install the Redwood SDK and run the sample app locally.
   - Python: pip install redwood-sdk; set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var; run python sample_app/quickstart.py
   - TypeScript: npm install @redwood/inference; export REDWOOD_API_KEY; yarn start:quickstart
2) Auth & local testing  start with API keys for POC; switch to service account + scoped keys for CI/production.
3) Routing & model pinning  pin the reranker to a low-latency variant for interactive calls; use the full-rank model for batch jobs.
4) Embeddings & reranker  build a simple vector store (we provide examples using FAISS/SQLite) and call our embeddings endpoint for upserts/query vectors.
5) Follow-up deep-dive  technical session with your infra engineer + our infra/SDK engineer (suggest Wed/Thu next week).

Attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (step-by-step), sample-apps.zip (python/ts quickstarts). Also linking the quickstart docs and sample repo below.

If you want, I can loop in our SDK engineer (Dev Patel) to walk through authentication patterns and local compose setups. What time works for a 45-min deep-dive next week?

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Alex  great questions, answered inline below. Looping in Dev (our SDK/infra engineer) to pick up the deep-dive and any follow-up notes.

1) Auth model:
- Yes  short-lived tokens via a service-account exchange are supported. We provide an STS-style flow: create a service account in the Redwood Console, mint a long-lived service credential in your control plane, then exchange it for scoped short-lived tokens via the token endpoint. Example snippets attached in env-setup-checklist.md.

2) Local testing:
- Recommended: run the sample app + a local proxy that forwards to Redwood for remote models, or run a small subset in Docker for offline prompt iteration. 
- We provide a docker-compose example (redwood-docker-compose.yml) that boots the sample app and a local FAISS index for retrieval. No license limits on the quickstart client, but open-model binaries are subject to their own licenses  sample-apps zip indicates which models are used.

3) Function/tool calling & structured output:
- You can declare an output schema in the SDK call and Redwood will validate structured outputs against the schema before returning them (schema validation errors are surfaced). For ticketing, you can request a JSON object with the fields you need; we also support function/tool annotations for automatic invocation.

4) Embeddings & reranker ops:
- For low-latency queries: keep your vector store local (FAISS) or colocated with your inference nodes. Incremental upserts are fine  batch them every few minutes for throughput efficiency, but do immediate upserts for critical items. Reranker should be a small low-latency model (quantized where possible)  we'll share recommended configs.

Proposed time: Wed May 13 at 1:30pm PST  does that work? Dev, can you take the call and walk through auth/docker/quickstart?

I attached env-setup-checklist.md that has the command lines and small code snippets for both Python and TypeScript quickstarts.

Thanks  Marissa

Hi Alex / Priya  looking forward to the deep-dive. A few pragmatic notes and quick commands to get you unstuck while we prepare the call.

Local quickstart (Python):
1) Create a virtualenv + install:
   python -m venv .venv
   source .venv/bin/activate
   pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0
2) Set credentials: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-api-key>"
3) Run sample app: python sample_app/quickstart.py --model=redwood-chat-small --streaming

TypeScript quickstart (Node 18+):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps.git
2) cd sample-apps/quickstart-ts
3) yarn install
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-api-key>"
5) yarn start

Docker / local compose note:
- We include a docker-compose file that starts a small FAISS service and the sample app. To run: docker compose -f redwood-docker-compose.yml up --build

Auth snippet (service account exchange):
- Exchange long-lived service credential for short-lived token:
   curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/token \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"service_credential":"<long-lived-cred>", "scope":"sdk:write sdk:embeddings"}'
- The response contains access_token + expires_in; use access_token for REDWOOD_AUTH_BEARER header.

Routing & model pinning:
- You can specify model and routing policy per-request:
   client.requests.create({ model: "redwood-chat-small-v2", routing: { region: "us-west", fallback: "redwood-chat-tiny" } })
- For latency SLOs, pin to a dedicated pool or use the low-latency variants we publish in the catalog.

Embeddings + reranker ops:
- Use batch upserts for bulk ingestion: POST /embeddings/upsert with up to 10k vectors per call (we recommend 1k-5k for stability).
- For live updates, single-item upserts are fine; be mindful of vector store shard placement for locality.

Additional resources we will cover on the call: sample repo walkthrough, env checklist, DAG of routing/fallback, and recommended quantization profiles for rerankers.
